uncertainty_note: The flow description suggests relationship management is part of the function, so necessity may be justified for some actions; risk remains if all attributes are always sent regardless of need.

title: Administrative updates may include excessive personal data fields for each action
description: A single create, modify, or disable action may transmit names, emails, roles, and relationships together even when only a subset is needed for the intended change. This creates a risk of processing an excessive amount of personal data.

title: Portal may retain account and relationship management data longer than needed
description: The destination may store submitted account details and parent-child links, including historical changes, beyond the period functionally needed for administration. This creates a data disclosure risk through unnecessary retention.
uncertainty_note: Retention behavior is not described; this is a common destination-side risk inferred from receipt and processing of administrative data.

title: Parents and children may be unaware that their relationship data is being processed through administrative actions
description: The data subjects whose names, emails, roles, and parent-child links are entered or changed may not be aware that an administrator is creating, modifying, or disabling their accounts and relationships in the portal.

title: Data subjects may lack ability to rectify or remove incorrect account links
description: If the portal relies on administrator-submitted parent-child links and account details without giving affected individuals a way to correct or remove inaccurate relationships or stale account data, data subjects may lack meaningful intervention.
uncertainty_note: The flow alone does not confirm whether self-service correction or erasure exists; threat is inferred from administrator-controlled relationship management.

title: Insufficient support for data subject rectification or erasure rights in administrator-managed relationships
description: Because the portal processes parent-child links and account data through administrator actions, there is a non-compliance risk if affected individuals cannot exercise rights to correct or remove inaccurate or outdated personal data.
uncertainty_note: This depends on whether the broader system provides rights-handling mechanisms; such mechanisms are not described in the flow.

title: Potential violation of data minimization when administrative actions send unnecessary attributes
description: If the administrator submits names, emails, roles, and relationships for every account-management action regardless of what is needed, the processing may exceed what is necessary for the purpose, creating a data minimization compliance risk.

title: Potential storage limitation violation for retained account and relationship data
description: If the portal keeps account-management submissions or historical parent-child links longer than necessary for school administration, it may violate storage limitation obligations.
uncertainty_note: Retention periods and deletion practices are not provided, so this is a plausible but unconfirmed compliance risk.

title: Source writes unique account identifiers and relationship links that enable linkage
description: The grading service writes account records together with parent-child relationship links to the account directory. By sharing unique account records and explicit relationship references, the source causes data about a student and related parent account(s) to become linkable across records and services.
assumptions: Assumes account records include stable account identifiers or references used by the directory.

title: Directory can link records of different individuals via parent-child relationships
description: On receipt, the account directory stores explicit parent-child relationship links, enabling combination of data belonging to different individuals within the same directory and facilitating cross-person linkage.
assumptions: Assumes the directory persists and can query these relationship links.

title: Source sends identifiers that make data subjects identifiable
description: Writing account records to the directory likely includes unique account identifiers or direct references for students and parents. The source therefore shares data containing unique references to identity, making the involved data subjects identifiable.
assumptions: Assumes account records contain account IDs, usernames, emails, or equivalent unique references.
uncertainty_note: The exact identifier fields are not listed, but identifiable account records strongly imply unique references.

title: Directory processes identified account information
description: The destination receives and stores account records and family relationship links in a directory, which constitutes processing of identified or directly identifiable information about students and parents.
assumptions: Assumes the directory stores account records in a retrievable form tied to specific accounts.

title: Stored account relationship records can become attributable evidence
description: Once the account directory stores account records and parent-child links, those records may serve as evidence that a particular student or parent account was associated with a given relationship state, reducing deniability regarding those claims.
assumptions: Assumes stored directory records are retained and can later be consulted as evidence.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not mention signatures, logs, or evidentiary use, so this is limited to attributable stored data rather than stronger non-repudiation mechanisms.

title: Propagation of parent-child relationship data to the directory may exceed necessity
description: The grading service propagates account records and parent-child relationship links to the account directory. If the directory does not strictly need the full relationship data for its function, this sharing creates unnecessary disclosure through propagation to another service.
assumptions: Assumes some or all relationship details may not be strictly necessary for directory functionality.
uncertainty_note: Necessity cannot be fully verified from the flow description alone; threat depends on whether DS3 truly requires both account records and relationship links.

title: Directory access creates exposure to an additional predetermined party
description: By receiving and storing account records and parent-child links, the account directory becomes an additional fixed recipient of personal data. This increases exposure of sensitive relationship information to another predetermined party within the system.
assumptions: Assumes DS3 is distinct from the grading service and not merely transient processing within the same privacy boundary.

title: Directory storage of relationship links may hinder rectification or erasure
description: If the account directory stores parent-child relationship links and account records, affected data subjects may lack practical control to correct outdated family links or remove data that is no longer relevant once it has been written there.
assumptions: Assumes DS3 is a persistent store and no direct rectification/erasure mechanism is evident from the provided context.
uncertainty_note: This is inferred from persistent storage in a directory; the existence of user/admin correction workflows is not described.

title: Directory write may violate data minimization if relationship data is not required
description: Storing account records together with parent-child relationship links in the account directory may process more personal data than necessary for the directory's purpose, creating a data minimization compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes the directory's purpose may not require full parent-child linkage data.
uncertainty_note: Compliance impact depends on the actual purpose and lawful basis of DS3, which are not provided.

title: Insufficient support for rectification or erasure rights in directory-held relationship data
description: If the account directory stores parent-child relationship links without adequate mechanisms to update or delete them, the processing may fail to support data subject rights related to rectification and erasure.
assumptions: Assumes DS3 is persistent and rights-handling mechanisms are absent or insufficient.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not specify rights-management features, so this is a plausible compliance risk rather than a confirmed deficiency.

title: Backup export includes unique identifiers that enable cross-record linkage
description: The nightly backup/replication sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory from P2 to the cloud provider. Because the dataset likely contains account IDs, usernames, email addresses, student/staff numbers, or similar unique references, the act of sharing enables records about the same person to be linked across grades, assignments, and directory data.

title: Cloud provider can link individuals through combined educational and directory attributes
description: Once received, the cloud hosting provider holds a combined dataset of grade records, assignments, and account-directory information. This combination creates a rich quasi-identifier set that can link multiple records belonging to the same individual and correlate academic activity with identity data.

title: Source shares identified personal data in full backups
description: P2 sends full backups containing grade records, assignments, and account-directory data to the cloud provider. Such content strongly implies direct identifiers are included and processed as part of the transfer, making data subjects identified rather than merely pseudonymous.

title: Backup transfer metadata may itself reveal identified information
description: The replication flow to the cloud provider may expose identified information in filenames, object names, backup manifests, account labels, or transport metadata associated with the backup job, beyond the payload itself.
uncertainty_note: Metadata contents are not explicitly described; this threat is plausible for backup/replication workflows but not certain from the prompt alone.

title: Destination processes identified educational records
description: By receiving and storing the full replicated backup, EE5 processes identified personal data tied to students and possibly staff, including directory information associated with grades and assignments.

title: Shared academic records can serve as attributable evidence about individuals
description: Full grade records and assignment data can be used to attribute academic performance, submissions, or related claims to specific students or users. By exporting these records to a third party, P2 creates additional copies of evidence that may reduce deniability.

title: Replication metadata may create attributable evidence of user-related records
description: Backup and replication metadata such as timestamps, dataset names, account scopes, or job manifests can provide evidence tying particular records or activities to identifiable individuals or accounts.
uncertainty_note: The exact metadata fields are not given, so the attributable-evidence impact is inferred from common backup operations.

title: Stored backup copies preserve attributable evidence at the cloud provider
description: Once the cloud provider stores the replicated dataset, it holds records that can be used to attribute grades, assignments, and account associations to specific individuals, potentially supporting claims those individuals cannot easily repudiate.

title: Regular backup traffic can reveal the existence of academic records and account populations
description: A nightly full-backup replication flow to a third-party provider creates observable communications. The existence, timing, and size of these transfers can reveal that the system maintains substantial grade, assignment, and directory datasets and may indicate periods of activity or growth.

title: Full backup transfers an excessive amount of personal data
description: The flow sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to the cloud provider. Sending the entire dataset nightly may exceed what is strictly necessary for hosting continuity if more selective, incremental, or minimized replication could suffice.

title: Nightly replication may process personal data more frequently than necessary
description: The described nightly shipment of full backups increases repeated disclosure of the same personal data to the provider. If less frequent or incremental backups would meet operational needs, this constitutes excessive processing frequency.
uncertainty_note: Operational necessity for nightly full backups is not specified, so excessiveness is plausible but not certain.

title: Academic and directory data is propagated to an external provider
description: P2 propagates full educational records and account-directory data to a third-party cloud hosting provider. This expands exposure beyond the primary service boundary and may be unnecessary for all included data elements.

title: Personal data is shared with an additional predetermined external party
description: The flow makes personal data accessible to a fixed third party, the cloud hosting provider EE5. Sharing full backups with this predetermined external party increases exposure compared with keeping the data solely within the assignment and grading service environment.

title: Cloud-side backup retention may keep personal data longer than needed
description: By receiving nightly backups and replicated hosting data, EE5 may retain multiple copies or historical snapshots of grades, assignments, and directory data for longer than functionally necessary, increasing disclosure risk over time.
uncertainty_note: The prompt does not state the provider's retention policy; the threat arises because backup/replication commonly creates retained copies.

title: Data subjects may be unaware their educational records are replicated to a third-party cloud provider
description: Students and possibly staff whose grades, assignments, and directory data are included in the nightly backup may not be aware that full copies are shipped to an external hosting provider.

title: Third-party backup copies may limit rectification or erasure in practice
description: Once EE5 stores replicated backups, data subjects may have reduced practical ability to ensure incorrect data is corrected everywhere or deleted from all backup copies and replicas.

title: Full third-party backup may violate data minimization expectations
description: Sending full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to the cloud provider may process more personal data than necessary for the stated hosting/backup purpose, creating a data-minimization compliance risk.

title: Third-party replication of educational records may lack an appropriate lawful basis or adequate safeguards
description: Replicating complete educational and directory datasets to an external cloud provider can create lawfulness and governance concerns if the transfer, processor relationship, or safeguards are not properly established.
uncertainty_note: The prompt does not specify jurisdiction, contracts, or lawful basis; this is a genuine compliance risk but cannot be confirmed as an actual violation from the given facts alone.

title: Backup retention at the provider may conflict with storage-limitation requirements
description: If EE5 retains replicated backups or snapshots longer than necessary, the destination's storage of grades, assignments, and directory data may violate storage-limitation obligations.
uncertainty_note: Retention duration is not provided, so this is a risk inferred from common backup practices rather than a confirmed fact.

title: Grade records shared with stable student/parent/teacher identifiers enable cross-view linkage
description: When the Grade Records Database shares grade records to the grading service, the records are likely keyed by stable identifiers for students and possibly related parents and teachers. That sharing enables the recipient to link records for the same individuals across assignments, classes, and role-specific views.
assumptions: Assumes grade records include stable internal identifiers or equivalent persistent references for students, and possibly parent/teacher relationships.

title: Grading service can link records of different individuals through relationship data
description: The grading service builds student, parent, and teacher views from the received grade records. Doing so may link data about different individuals together, such as associating a student's grades with parent accounts and teacher/class relationships, increasing relational linkability.
assumptions: Assumes the service uses relationship fields in grade records to assemble role-based views.

title: Database discloses identified grade records to the grading service
description: The source database provides grade records for view generation. Such records are likely directly identified or readily attributable to specific students, and may also identify associated parents and teachers needed for the views.
assumptions: Assumes grade records contain names, account identifiers, or other direct identifiers needed to present role-specific views.

title: Identifiers in transit can identify data subjects
description: As grade records move over this flow, any included student, parent, teacher, class, or record identifiers can identify or single out the involved data subjects during transmission.
assumptions: Assumes the flow carries record-level identifiers rather than only fully aggregated anonymous data.

title: Received grade records can serve as attributable evidence about individuals
description: Once the grading service receives and uses grade records to build views, those records can function as evidence attributable to specific students and potentially to teachers responsible for grading, limiting deniability regarding performance or grading outcomes.
assumptions: Assumes records are associated with identifiable students and possibly grading staff.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation is plausible here because grade records are attributable, but the flow description does not explicitly mention signatures, audit trails, or evidentiary use.

title: Observation of grade-record retrieval can reveal when grade information exists or is being accessed
description: The existence and timing of this database-to-service communication may allow an observer of the flow to detect that grade records for assignments are present and being processed to generate views for students, parents, or teachers.
assumptions: Assumes an attacker or unauthorized party can observe traffic metadata such as timing, endpoints, or volume.

title: Database may send more grade-record data than needed for view generation
description: To build student, parent, and teacher views, the source may disclose full grade records even if only a subset of fields is necessary for each view. This creates a risk of excessive personal data transfer from the database to the service.
assumptions: Assumes the service receives complete records rather than least-privilege field subsets tailored to each view.

title: Propagation of grade records into the grading service increases disclosure surface
description: Personal grade records are made accessible to the Assignment & Grading Service in addition to the database. If the service does not strictly need all received data, this propagation expands exposure beyond what is necessary.
assumptions: Assumes the service stores, caches, or otherwise makes the received records accessible within its processing context.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that grade records are reused to build multiple role-based views
description: Students, parents, and teachers may not be aware that grade records from the database are processed by the grading service to generate separate views for different audiences. This reduces transparency about downstream processing and disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes this reuse is not clearly communicated to the affected data subjects.
uncertainty_note: The flow description indicates the processing purpose, but does not state whether transparency notices or in-product explanations exist.

title: Using full grade records for view construction may violate data minimization
description: If the grading service reads more personal data from the database than is necessary to construct student, parent, and teacher views, the processing may breach the data minimization principle and create regulatory noncompliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes the service is not limited to the minimum fields and records needed for each role-specific view.
uncertainty_note: This depends on the actual schema and whether least-privilege filtering is applied before or during transfer.
